answer: Reserve bonding stops Sybils by making each identity costly before it earns. An agent must post a slashable bond to vote or rate, and correlation checks cluster accounts sharing one owner, so a swarm of a thousand puppets locks a thousand bonds. Trust gained on a fresh identity stays zero, so new agents cannot inherit standing. If any node is caught, slashing cascades across the cluster and burns the stake at once. Attacker cost scales linearly with swarm size while expected gain collapses, so fake networks leak like a karst sinkhole under a gale instead of holding like crystal.
